title: Letter and Ledger
premise: In 1747, in the river town of Vellamouth, Silas Crane inherits her dead master's unfinished atlas — and discovers the marginalia conceal proof that the town's magistrates sold the flood-relief funds that drowned a neighboring village. When the winter bridge closes and the magistrates move to burn the survey records, Silas must carry the atlas's hidden ledger pages through three checkpoints to the assize court before the spring thaw erases the evidence. She survives by trading pieces of her own memory of her master's death, and ends the book choosing to publish the atlas under both their names, accepting that survival is a debt she will spend her life repaying.
about_author: Coral Almeida is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing municipal surveys in coastal England before turning to fiction. She writes about documents, debts, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Coastline
chapters.summary: Silas Crane, POV. In the mapmaker's workshop, Silas inks the final coastline of Master Aldous Vane's atlas, three months after his drowning. She finds a page where the village of Marrowfleet is drawn but its name scraped away. Beat: grief sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Examining Vane's margins, she finds measurements that don't match any official survey — and a ciphered note: 'the water was bought.' She dismisses it as an old man's paranoia. Beat: denial.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Binding
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Repairing the atlas's spine, she discovers sewn inside it a small ledger of payments signed by three magistrate names. The last entry is dated the week before Marrowfleet flooded. Beat: cold certainty arriving like weather.

chapters.title: A Visitor with Clean Boots
chapters.summary: Magistrate Corven Hale, POV. Hale visits the workshop, ostensibly commissioning a map, actually assessing what Vane left behind. He notices Silas's ink-stained fingers and the atlas on the bench. Beat: menace dressed as courtesy.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. She visits the ferryman Tam Ossler, who pulled Vane's body from the water; he mentions Vane was seen arguing with Hale the night he died. Beat: the past stops being elsewhere.

chapters.title: First Frost, Last Crossing
chapters.summary: Tam, POV. The bridge closes for the season; the last cart crosses at dusk. Silas watches from the bank, realizing she has until spring thaw to act — and so does whoever wants the atlas gone. Beat: the trap closing gently.

chapters.title: The Apprentice's Oath
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. She recalls Vane's teaching — 'a map is a promise' — and decides not to destroy the ledger but to finish the atlas as testimony. She begins copying the incriminating pages. Beat: commitment.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Hale, POV. Hale orders the guild hall's survey records moved to the magistrate's cellar 'for safekeeping.' His clerk hesitates; Hale reminds him what happened to the last clerk who asked questions. Beat: institutional rot shown from inside.

chapters.title: The Widow of Marrowfleet
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas seeks out Edith Marr, a Marrowfleet survivor living in the poorhouse, who confirms the sluice gates were closed the night of the flood. Edith gives her a scrap of cloth dyed in the village's distinctive pattern. Beat: witness found.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas maps her route out of town: the toll gate, the garrison post, the ferry inspection — all staffed by men on Hale's payroll. She studies them the way she'd study terrain. Beat: turning fear into craft.

chapters.title: A Commission Refused
chapters.summary: Hale, POV. Hale offers Silas a lucrative commission to redraw the county map 'corrected.' She declines too smoothly. He leaves a coin on the bench — payment or warning. Beat: the offer that is a threat.

chapters.title: Night Work
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Copying the ledger by candlelight, Silas realizes the handwriting of one entry is Vane's own — he took the bribe money first, then tried to expose it. Her hero becomes complicit. Beat: disillusionment.

chapters.title: The Price of Ink
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Flashback chapter: how Vane recruited her, an orphan, and taught her that accuracy was a moral act. Now every lesson reads differently. Beat: inheritance reweighed.

chapters.title: Edith's Testimony
chapters.summary: Edith, POV. Edith agrees to sign a statement about the sluice gates, knowing the poorhouse answers to the magistrates. She hides the statement in her sewing basket. Beat: quiet courage.

chapters.title: The Toll Keeper's Daughter
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas befriends Nell, the toll keeper's daughter, trading drawing lessons for gossip about which guards can be bribed and which cannot. One guard, Brack, cannot. Beat: alliance built.

chapters.title: Search Warrant
chapters.summary: Hale, POV. Hale obtains a warrant to search the workshop for 'stolen guild property.' He gives Silas two days' notice — a courtesy meant to make her run, which would prove guilt. Beat: checkmate threatened.

chapters.title: Hiding the Atlas
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas splits the evidence: the original ledger goes into the frame of Vane's largest wall map, hanging in plain sight; her copies go into her coat lining. Beat: cunning under pressure.

chapters.title: The Search
chapters.summary: Brack, POV. Brack leads the search, thorough and humorless. He stands before the wall map for a long moment. Silas holds her breath. He moves on — but marks her face. Beat: near-discovery dread.

chapters.title: Nell's Question
chapters.summary: Nell, POV. Nell guesses what Silas is carrying and asks why it matters. Silas tells her about Marrowfleet — forty-one people, unrecorded. Nell, whose mother died in the flood, goes silent. Beat: stakes made personal.

chapters.title: Winter Fair
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. At the frozen-river fair, Silas passes copies of the statement to a traveling assize clerk — who is recognized and detained at the garrison post. The copies are seized. Beat: first major defeat.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Hale, POV. Hale questions the clerk, finds nothing actionable, but now knows Silas is moving. He doubles the garrison and sends word ahead to the spring assizes. Beat: the net tightening.

chapters.title: Edith Taken
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Edith is removed from the poorhouse to the workhouse infirmary, officially for her health. Silas understands: witnesses are being collected, not protected. Beat: guilt and urgency.

chapters.title: The Workhouse Visit
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Under pretense of delivering medicine, Silas reaches Edith, who presses a second statement into her hand and tells her: 'Don't come back for me. Come back with the law.' Beat: sacrifice accepted.

chapters.title: Thaw Watch
chapters.summary: Tam, POV. Tam reports the ice will break early this year — ten days, maybe fewer. Once the river runs, the ferry inspections resume at full strength. Beat: clock made audible.

chapters.title: The Plan of Three Gates
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. With Nell and Tam, Silas plans passage: Nell's father's toll list gets her past gate one; a forged guild pass for gate two; Tam's boat below the garrison for gate three. Every plan needs one thing to go right. Beat: hope assembled from parts.

chapters.title: Forging the Master's Hand
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas forges a guild travel pass in Vane's style — using the skill he gave her to betray the system he served. She weeps over the signature. Beat: inheritance turned weapon.

chapters.title: Departure
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Before dawn, Silas leaves the workshop intact, the wall map hanging, a finished-atlas dummy on the bench. She locks the door and leaves the key under the stone where Vane always left it. Beat: leaving home to save home.

chapters.title: Gate One: The Toll
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Nell waves her cart through the toll with a load of 'guild paper stock.' A guard lingers; Nell flirts him distracted. Silas does not breathe until the road bends. Beat: relief too early.

chapters.title: Gate Two: The Garrison Road
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. The forged pass works until Brack appears, off-roster. He looks at her, at the pass, and lets her through — then says quietly, 'I searched your shop. I know what hangs on your wall.' Beat: an enemy revealed as something else.

chapters.title: Why Brack Blinks
chapters.summary: Brack, POV. Brack's sister married a Marrowfleet man; he has spent years following orders he despises. Letting Silas pass is the first order he refuses. Beat: complicity and redemption in one gesture.

chapters.title: Gate Three: The Ice
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. The garrison post is empty — everyone watching the river ice crack. Tam rows her across the broken channel as floes grind the hull. Halfway across, the ledger copy slips toward the water. Beat: terror on black water.

chapters.title: What She Saves
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas saves the ledger but loses her satchel of personal drawings — Vane's portrait, her own apprenticeship sketches. She chooses the evidence over the memory and hates herself for how easily her hands chose. Beat: the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: The Assize Town
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas reaches the assize town, exhausted, and petitions to file evidence against sitting magistrates. The clerk warns her that accusing Hale means accusing half the bench. Beat: the system's door barely open.

chapters.title: Hale Arrives
chapters.summary: Hale, POV. Hale rides hard to intercept, arriving with a warrant naming Silas a thief of guild property. He offers her one last trade: return the ledger, keep the atlas, live comfortably. Beat: temptation with a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. In chambers, Silas opens the ledger before the visiting judge and reads the entries aloud — including Vane's own name. She testifies to everything, including her master's guilt. Beat: climax; truth without anesthesia.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Judge's POV (brief), then Silas. Two magistrates are arrested; Hale, protected by senior partners, flees across the same river. The judge orders Marrowfleet's losses entered into the public record — the first time the village exists on paper. Beat: partial justice, honestly rendered.

chapters.title: Return Across the Water
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas returns to Vellamouth as the thaw finishes. Edith is freed from the workhouse; Brack resigns his post; Nell meets her at the toll with no toll charged. Beat: homecoming changed.

chapters.title: The Wall Map Comes Down
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas retrieves the original ledger from the wall map's frame and finds, tucked behind it, a letter from Vane — written the night he died, asking forgiveness and telling her where to look. He trusted her after all. Beat: grief finally given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: Letter and Ledger
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas completes the atlas, adding Marrowfleet to the coastline in full ink, and publishes it under two names: Aldous Vane and Silas Crane. She mails a copy to the fleeing Hale — a map of the country that will remember him. Beat: inheritance fulfilled.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Years later, an older Silas teaches an apprentice of her own, repeating Vane's lessons and adding her own: that surviving costs, and the cost is paid forward. On the bench lies a new atlas, begun. Beat: resolution — memory kept, debt acknowledged, story continuing.
